impact_assessment.benefits: every printed or documented python command in AIKit resolves; a moved entry point fails --check instead of shipping dead hints
impact_assessment.risks: contract: --check gains a failure class; dependency: none (stdlib re, git ls-files); concurrency: none, read-only scan; state: none written

[1/2] Shared marked-block helper; media README markers use it unchanged. [2/2] License section writes its generated paragraph between aegean:license markers and later refreshes replace only that (IDEA-398)

impact_assessment.why: a license switch replaces everything from the License heading to the next ## heading, so a user's own subsection there is deleted; three past fixes (4ec9ffa, 3c3b23c, 38bc4e6) were generators overwriting user content
impact_assessment.benefits: text a user adds around AIKit's generated license paragraph survives every refresh; one marker helper instead of three hand-written copies in project_media
impact_assessment.risks: contract: README gains two invisible HTML comments in the License section; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: existing READMEs migrate once via the old heading match
impact_assessment.mitigation: fall back to the current heading regex when markers are absent so existing READMEs keep working; failing-first test for a user subsection surviving a second switch; media refactor covered by its existing tests

[1/1] verify_commit warns when a commit leaves a modified file under half its parent size (>=400 bytes), unless the message says shrink-ok: <reason> (IDEA-262)

impact_assessment.why: an overwritten file looks like an ordinary edit to every gate; the README rewrite repaired in 4ec9ffa is the recorded case, and PRINCIPLE-013 treats lost content as data loss
impact_assessment.benefits: a commit that silently drops most of a file is named with both sizes before the push, while R5's cheap undo still applies
impact_assessment.risks: contract: verify_commit output gains WARN lines, exit code unchanged; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: read-only git object reads (3 calls)
impact_assessment.mitigation: warn, never block (the R3 gate list and principle text stay as they are); ignore files under 400 bytes and added/deleted files; shrink-ok reason in the message clears it; measure the warning rate over recent history before finishing

[1/1] update_knowledge_base.py --digest prints one line per module (path, lines, classes/functions, purpose) within 100 lines and 16k chars, shared-code folders first, ending with an explicit truncated: line (IDEA-005, absorbs IDEA-044/077)

impact_assessment.why: knowledge/codebase_map.md is 2,275 lines / 150 KB (neurocore's 6,872), far past the 100-line read and 16k-char payload rules (PRINCIPLE-004/012), so a cold-start agent cannot read the map it is told to use
impact_assessment.benefits: one bounded read orients an agent in any workspace; truncation is stated, never silent
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new read-only flag, no file written, no existing output changes; dependency: none (existing AST extractor); concurrency: none; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: pure build_digest with unit tests for budget, ordering, truncation and determinism; --digest prints and exits before any write path

impact_assessment.benefits: every skill trigger loads about half the text; project and delegation detail is read only when that work starts
impact_assessment.risks: contract: hosts that load SKILL.md see less inline and must open a topic file; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: two new mirrored files
impact_assessment.mitigation: binding one-line project rules stay in SKILL.md; topic files are mirrored by the same generator and checked by sync --check; a test bounds SKILL.md and requires every named topic file in both skill folders; citation test covers the new files
